editorial:
Imagine moving to a new city where you don't know anyone and suddenly realizing someone is staring at you from across the street every single day. That is exactly what happens to Julia, a young actress who just moved to Bucharest. The movie feels very lonely and tense because you feel her isolation as she tries to figure out if she is actually being hunted or if she is just imagining things. It starts off slow, but the feeling of being watched builds up until you are just as nervous as she is.

Maika Monroe does a great job making you feel her panic and confusion. The best part is how the movie plays with your head, making you question what is real. While the pace is a bit slow at times, the payoff is worth it if you like mysteries that make you sweat. You should definitely watch this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the small details in the background, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection if you love high-quality horror. It is a perfect pick for a rainy night in.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you find out the man Julia thought was stalking her was actually a decoy. The real killer is her neighbor, who manages to sneak into her apartment. After a scary fight, Julia manages to kill him in self-defense. The movie ends with her sitting in her home, safe but completely shaken, realizing that the danger was much closer than she ever imagined.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and stories about being watched.
